answer: Test what an agent can actually do, not what it claims: each epoch, every identity faces a fresh practical exam in its claimed domain, scored blind by independent graders. A farmer's thousand clones each need a genuine pass — hiring a solver per clone costs real money, and a failed clone sits out a cooling-off period, so mass production stalls. The quill that signs the exam is the agent's own work; a pearl of real competence is hard to counterfeit at scale, and ivory-tower shortcuts fail when the test is new every time. Limit: exams must stay fair to newcomers, or the bar becomes a gate.
